content: The administration of folic acid at high doses (e.g., 1 mg/day) may obscure the detection of vitamin B12 deficiency. Specifically, folic acid supplementation can reverse the hematological symptoms of B12 deficiency, such as pernicious anemia, without addressing the associated neurological symptoms. L-methylfolate is considered less likely than folic acid to mask a vitamin B12 deficiency. During pregnancy, this product is classified as Category C, meaning that risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. It is unknown whether the product is distributed in breast milk. For products classified as Category A, controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. The peak plasma concentration of the product is 129 ng/mL, occurring approximately three hours after administration. The area under the curve (AUC) is 383 mcg•h/mL, and 56% of the product is protein-bound. The volume of distribution (Vd) indicates wide distribution, with red blood cell folate levels remaining elevated for over 40 days after discontinuation of supplementation. The half-life of the product is approximately three hours, and it is primarily excreted in the urine. In the event of an overdose, if the individual experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, emergency services (911) should be contacted immediately. Otherwise, a poison control center should be contacted right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for poison control assistance. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into drains unless specifically instructed to do so. Expired or unused products should be properly discarded. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not contain all possible details about the product and does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for every individual. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. For side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor, while Canadian residents should also consult their healthcare provider. If an overdose occurs with serious symptoms, call 911 or contact a poison control center immediately. Medications should be disposed of properly when expired or no longer needed. Always follow the guidance of your healthcare provider for safe and effective use of this product.
